candidate.answerReason: The smallest product with one negative factor is (-8)(5)(7) = -280. Using all three negative numbers gives -192, and nonnegative products are larger.

methods.label: Compare the possible negative products
methods.explanation:
A negative product is possible, so a zero or positive product cannot be the minimum. Three nonzero factors have a negative product exactly when one or three of them are negative.

With one negative factor, we want the greatest possible magnitude, because a negative number with greater magnitude is smaller. The negative factor has magnitude at most \(8\), and the two largest distinct positive factors are \(5\) and \(7\). Thus the smallest product in this case is
\[
(-8)(5)(7)=-280.
\]
With three negative factors, we must use all three negative numbers in the set, giving
\[
(-8)(-6)(-4)=-192.
\]
These cases cover every negative product. Since \(-280<-192\), the minimum possible product is \(\boxed{-280}\), choice B.
methods.levelReason: The argument uses signed integer products and comparison, with a complete split into the possible negative-product cases.
